title: Module Assessment: Context Managers & Resources (PY_230 to PY_236)

slides.title: Module 5 Overview
slides.prompt: Assessment covering the `with` statement, __enter__ / __exit__ protocols, @contextmanager, ExitStack, and resource leak prevention.
slides.codeSnippet:
with open('file.txt', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

slides.title: Question 1: The 'with' Statement
slides.prompt: What is the primary purpose of the `with` statement in Python?
options: To ensure proper acquisition and release of resources, even if exceptions occur
To speed up file reading operations
slides.correctAnswer: To ensure proper acquisition and release of resources, even if exceptions occur

slides.title: Question 2: Magic Methods
slides.prompt: Which two dunder methods are required to implement a custom class-based context manager?

slides.title: Question 3: Enter Return Value
slides.prompt: In `with MyContext() as obj:`, the `obj` receives the return value of which magic method?

slides.title: Question 4: Suppressing Exceptions
slides.prompt: How can a context manager's `__exit__` method suppress an exception that occurred inside the `with` block?

slides.title: Question 5: Contextlib Decorator
slides.prompt: Fill in the decorator used to turn a generator function into a context manager.

slides.title: Question 6: Generator Context Manager
slides.prompt: When using `@contextmanager`, what separates the setup code from the teardown code?

slides.title: Question 7: Handling Multiple Contexts
slides.prompt: Which tool from `contextlib` is designed to programmatically manage a dynamic number of context managers?

slides.title: Question 8: Async Context
slides.prompt: Fill in the syntax to enter an asynchronous context manager.

slides.title: Question 9: Async Magic Methods
slides.prompt: Which methods are required for an ASYNCHRONOUS context manager?

slides.title: Question 10: Suppressing specific errors
slides.prompt: Fill in the context manager from `contextlib` used to ignore specific exceptions temporarily.
slides.codeSnippet:
from contextlib import ___

with suppress(FileNotFoundError):
    os.remove('fake.txt')

slides.title: Question 11: Redirecting Output
slides.prompt: Which `contextlib` utility temporarily redirects `sys.stdout` to another file or stream?

slides.title: Question 12: Nested Contexts
slides.prompt: How can you open two files simultaneously in a single `with` statement in Python 3?
options: with open('a.txt') as a, open('b.txt') as b:
It is not possible without ExitStack
slides.correctAnswer: with open('a.txt') as a, open('b.txt') as b:

slides.title: Question 13: Reentrant Context Managers
options: It can be entered multiple times in nested with statements
It restarts the program upon exit
It executes in a loop automatically
slides.correctAnswer: It can be entered multiple times in nested with statements

slides.title: Question 14: Closing Utility
slides.prompt: Fill in the contextlib utility that calls `.close()` on an object upon exiting the block.
slides.codeSnippet:
from contextlib import ___

with closing(urllib.request.urlopen('http://url')) as page:
    pass
